Tentative Review - Updated 12-03-2015 - Currently we have a brand new Kuerig 2.0 - K500 brewer. I purchased this product (SoloPod) since it states that it is compatible with Kuerig 2.0 systems. What I found was the product is designed to accept either single or carafe size amounts for brewing in appropriately sized baskets. Either size must be placed in the carafe sized container before inserting in the brewer. When I did this (after being sure the clip that accompanies the product was installed correctly) the arm that is lowered into place in order to start the brewing process refused to close all the way. Being a new purchase I did not want to force the brewer and possibly break it. I must say that I am currently in communication with Solofill about this but after describing the situation to them in detail I received an email from someone who appears to not have read any of the previous emails and now wishes me to produce photographs of this issue. Something I feel is not my responsibility to provide. Either they sell a product that works with 2.0 systems or they don't. Hence the 3 stars until I get final resolution (one way or another) on this matter. When this happens I will update my review.

Update: As I have not heard back from Solofill after my last email to them mentioned above I have to assume that the correspondance relating to my initial complaint has been lost or they would just rather the problem go away. Either way the experience was very disappointing from a customer service perspective and also from the money wasted. I am lowering this review to one star.

Further Update (12-3-2015): After off and on fiddling with this product it is finally working with our Keurig 2.0. I have upped the rating to 4 stars but I would still give the maker, Solofill, one star or less for their almost non-existant customer service.

solved problem with unresponsive buttons - Buttons on my Jenn-Air Dishwasher became unresponsive so all I could do is start it. None of the options were accessible other than the 2 hour delay. I wondered if I needed to replace this button panel, or the circuit board it attaches to. I ordered this based on some internet research and the reviews indicating a solution to similar symptoms.

The item arrived and I quickly slipped the ribbon cable into the connector on the circuit board without removing the old panel. This test proved it would resolve the problem. I proceeded to replace the control panel in position. The only tools needed are a T-20 Torx driver, and a 1/4 hex-head capscrew driver (or 1/4 inch socket). Be sure to unplug the dishwasher since removing the circuit board cover exposes some 120V connectors that are not hard to short with a tool or your hand, hence the warning sticker on the cover.

Possibly the most amazing flaw is that, here in 2020, an oven with electronic controls does NOT include a timed cooking option. The oven has a timer, but it's just a timer; it beeps. It's on you to remember to turn your oven off or change the temperature or whatever. I find it hard to understand why anybody would bother to manufacture an oven control "brain" like that.

(edited) If you want to take advantage of the "Fit Promise" guarantee, it appears to be based on what the installer did to overcome the fit problem (whatever it might be). You'll need a photo of the previous oven while it was still installed, a picture of the empty alcove before the new oven is installed, and a picture of the newly-installed oven. You'll also need a receipt for whatever the installer did to overcome the fitting problem, which in my case was nothing so I get nothing.
